title: Tips & Tricks: 5 Simple Ways To Keep Coriander Leaves Fresh For A Week Without A Freezer
text:
Tips & Tricks: 5 Simple Ways To Keep Coriander Leaves Fresh For A Week Without A Freezer
Curated By :
Last Updated:
Coriander leaves spoil quickly because of their high moisture. Heat and air speed up the process, turning leaves yellow or black within days if not stored properly
Advertisement
1/11
Coriander leaves are a staple in kitchens across India, used in everything from green chutneys to garnishing vegetables and decorating parathas. Their aroma and flavour enhance any dish. However, the biggest challenge is their short shelf life. Within two days, these leaves often start wilting. Without a freezer or adequate space, coriander spoils even faster. Many people buy fresh coriander expecting it to last a week, only to find it turning black within 2-3 days, affecting taste and freshness. (News18 Hindi)
Advertisement
2/11
This leads to repeated trips to the market, creating irritation and extra expense. Fortunately, there are simple, cost-free methods to keep coriander green and fresh for a week without refrigeration. These traditional tricks are easy to follow and highly effective. (News18 Hindi)
3/11
Coriander spoils quickly due to its high moisture content. Heat and air accelerate this process, causing leaves to yellow or blacken within days. Storing coriander in closed polythene bags can trap moisture, leading to faster rotting. Adopting the right storage techniques is therefore essential. (News18 Hindi)
Advertisement
4/11
Trick 1: Wash the coriander gently with water and dry it thoroughly. Wrap the leaves in a cotton or muslin cloth and place them in a basket or lidded container. Protected from air, coriander can remain fresh for up to a week. (News18 Hindi)
5/11
Trick 2: Clay pots are still widely used in villages. Lightly wet the coriander and store it in a clay pot. The natural coolness of the clay helps preserve freshness for longer periods. (News18 Hindi)
Advertisement
6/11
Trick 3: Place washed coriander in a lidded pot along with lemon peel. The peel prevents bacterial growth and helps maintain the colour and freshness of the leaves. (News18 Hindi)
7/11
Trick 4: Coriander often comes with roots attached. Keep the roots covered with lightly damp soil and a cloth. This method helps maintain leaf freshness for a week without refrigeration. (News18 Hindi)
Advertisement
8/11
Trick 5: If a fridge is unavailable, wrapping dry coriander in newspaper and storing it in a dry box works effectively. The newspaper absorbs excess moisture, keeping the leaves fresh longer. (News18 Hindi)
9/11
These simple, traditional methods save money and time by reducing the need for repeated market trips. They ensure that kitchens are always stocked with fragrant, fresh coriander. (News18 Hindi)
Advertisement
10/11
To ensure success, always wash coriander with clean water before storage. Avoid storing overly wet leaves and keep them away from direct sunlight. Cool, dry storage is ideal. If coriander has roots, it is best stored intact. (News18 Hindi)
